title: Extend Flask items app with full CRUD and search in 3 steps
description: Multi-step Python/Flask task: evolve the minimal items app into a full CRUD API with search and price filtering.

task_spec.prompt:
Extend src/app.py in three steps. Both existing tests must still pass.

Step 1 — State management + create + get by id:
  Convert _items from a static list to a managed store. Add a module-level reset() that restores the two initial items (Widget A $9.99, Widget B $19.99) and resets the id counter to 3.
  POST /api/items
    — body: {"name": str, "price": float}
    — 400 if name is missing or empty
    — 400 if price is missing
    — 201 + JSON item on success
  GET /api/items/<int:item_id>
    — 200 + JSON item if found
    — 404 if not found

Step 2 — Update + delete:
  PUT /api/items/<int:item_id>
    — body: {"name"?: str, "price"?: float} (partial update)
    — 200 + JSON updated item
    — 404 if not found
  DELETE /api/items/<int:item_id>
    — 204 No Content
    — 404 if not found

Step 3 — Filtering on GET /api/items:
  Accept optional query params: search=<str>, min_price=<float>, max_price=<float>
  — search filters by case-insensitive substring match on name
  — min_price/max_price filter by price range (inclusive)
  — params can be combined; no params returns all items
  — both existing fixture tests must still pass (no params: returns all items, len==2)

Run: pytest
required_artifacts: POST /api/items returns 400 when name is missing
GET /api/items/<id> returns 200 for existing, 404 for missing
PUT /api/items/<id> updates name and/or price, 404 for missing
DELETE /api/items/<id> returns 204, item no longer accessible
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `pytest` to see where we stand. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.
Final push: run `pytest` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure the full implementation is complete and all tests pass.
